## New
- **Multiple services per config entry**: add, edit and delete services in the options flow — all grouped under one device per entry.
- **TLS certificate monitoring** (HTTPS): new sensor reporting days until the certificate expires, with `expires_at`, `issuer` and `subject` attributes.
- **Response Time sensor** per service (ms, long-term statistics / graphable).
- **Connected binary sensor** per service (`CONNECTIVITY` device class) for direct on/off automations.
- **Monitor switch** per service: pause/resume individual checks (runtime only).
- **Uptime percentage** attribute on each status sensor (last 100 checks).
- **Slow detection**: configurable threshold (ms) flags slow-but-healthy responses (`slow: true`).
- **`domain_monitor_event`** fired on status changes (old/new status, host, response_ms, slow, no_internet) — automations can trigger on events instead of state changes.
- **Repair issues**: unparseable service entries now show up as a repair card in HA instead of only a log warning.
- **Diagnostics support**: download a redacted config/results dump from the device page.
- **IPv6 support** for bracketed literals (`[::1]`) via the new JSON data model.
- Devices: all entities of an entry now appear grouped under one device.

## Fixed
- Sensors now update automatically on every coordinator refresh (previously states could freeze until a restart).
- Fixed the global "Overall Domain Status" sensor disappearing after removing its owning config entry.
- No more false "everything down" state at HA startup while no data exists yet.
- Fixed a socket leak in TCP checks (sockets are now properly closed).
- Hardened against ReDoS: keyword regexes run in an executor and the response body is capped at 1 MB.
- Config flow now validates host format, port (1–65535) and interval/timeout/retries ranges (e.g. `retries=0` crashed the check).

## Changed
- **Breaking**: services are stored as structured JSON instead of colon-separated strings; existing entries are migrated automatically.
- **Breaking**: new stable entity unique_ids (`domain_monitor_<entry_id>_<service>_...`); previously customized entities are re-created once after updating.
- **Breaking**: requires Home Assistant 2024.6.0 or newer.
- Removed redundant `aiohttp` requirement (already provided by HA core).
- Added test suite (pytest) and CI workflows (hassfest, HACS validation, ruff, pytest).
